text: When the day of Pentecost finally came, they were all gathered together in the same place.
Suddenly a sound like a powerful rushing wind came down from the sky and filled the whole house where they were sitting.
Something resembling individual flames of fire appeared and came to rest on each one of them.
Every one of them was filled with the Holy Spirit and began speaking in other languages, exactly as the Spirit gave them the ability.
Now there were devout Jews living in Jerusalem at the time, drawn from every nation under the sky.
When this sound rang out, a crowd gathered, and they were thrown into confusion because each person heard the believers speaking in his own native language.
Astounded and amazed, they said, Aren't all these men speaking Galileans?
Then how is it that each of us hears them in the very language we were born into?
Parthians, Medes, and Elamites; residents of Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia,
Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, and the districts of Libya near Cyrene; travelers from Rome,
both Jews by birth and converts to Judaism; Cretans and Arabs — we hear them telling of God's great deeds, each in our own language!
They were all amazed and at a loss, asking each other, What can this possibly mean?
But some in the crowd mocked them, saying, They've simply had too much new wine.

Then Peter stood up together with the other eleven apostles, raised his voice, and spoke to the crowd: Fellow Jews and all of you staying in Jerusalem, let me make this clear to you; pay close attention to what I say.
These people aren't drunk, as you're assuming — it's only nine in the morning!
No, this is exactly what was announced through the prophet Joel:
God says, In the last days I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your young men will have visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
Even on my servants, both men and women, I will pour out my Spirit in those days, and they will prophesy.
I will display wonders in the sky above and signs on the ground below — blood, fire, and billows of smoke.
The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and glorious day of the Lord arrives.
And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.
Men of Israel, hear me: Jesus of Nazareth was a man clearly certified to you by God through the miracles, wonders, and signs God performed among you through him, as you yourselves already know.
This man was handed over to you according to God's determined plan and foreknowledge, and you, using the hands of lawless men, put him to death by nailing him to a cross.
But God raised him up, releasing him from the agony of death, because it was impossible for death to hold him in its grip.
David said concerning him, I kept the Lord always before me; because he stands at my right hand, I will not be moved.
That is why my heart was glad and my words full of joy; even my body will rest secure in hope,
because you will not leave my soul in the grave, nor will you let your holy one see decay.
You have shown me the paths of life; your presence will fill me with gladness.
Brothers, I can tell you plainly about our ancestor David that he died, was buried, and his tomb remains among us to this day.
But since he was a prophet, he knew God had sworn an oath to him that one of his own descendants would sit on his throne.
Seeing this in advance, he spoke of the Messiah's resurrection, that he was not left in the grave and his body never decayed.
God has raised this very Jesus back to life, and every one of us can testify to it.
Lifted up to God's right hand, he received the promised Holy Spirit from the Father and has poured out what you are now seeing and hearing.
David himself never ascended to heaven, and yet he said, The Lord said to my Lord, sit here at my right hand
until I place your enemies as a footstool beneath your feet.
So let all the house of Israel know beyond doubt: God has made this Jesus, the very one you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.
On hearing this, the people were stung to the heart and asked Peter and the rest of the apostles, Brothers, what are we supposed to do?
Peter replied, Turn from your sins and be baptized, each of you, in the name of Jesus the Messiah, and your sins will be forgiven; then you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
This promise is for you, for your children, and for everyone who is far away — for all whom the Lord our God calls to himself.
He kept on pleading with them at length, urging, Save yourselves from this crooked generation.
Those who welcomed his message were baptized, and about three thousand people were added to their number that day.
They gave themselves continually to the apostles' teaching, to fellowship together, to the sharing of meals, and to prayer.
A deep sense of awe fell on everyone, and many wonders and signs were being done through the apostles.
All who believed stayed united and held everything they owned in common.
They would sell their property and possessions and hand out the proceeds to whoever was in need.
Day by day they gathered together in the temple courts and shared meals in one another's homes, eating with glad and generous hearts,
praising God and enjoying the favor of everyone around them. And every day the Lord kept adding to their number those who were being saved.
